stages.name: Effects of inflation
stages.title: Effects of inflation
stages.sub: How a sustained rise in prices reshapes what workers, savers, borrowers and the government actually get.

steps.q: Your pay rises from £20,000 to £20,400 but prices rise 5%. Can you buy more, the same, or less than before?
steps.hint: Your pay went up 2%, but prices went up 5%. Which grew faster?
steps.pre: What your wage actually buys is called your

steps.q: Prices are rising fast and your buying power is falling. What is happening to you as a worker?
steps.right: You are worse off unless wages catch up
steps.wrong: You are automatically no worse off
steps.hint: You already found your real wage fell. Does a pay rise claim fix that on its own?
steps.pre: So inflation squeezes real income and pushes wage bargaining, which is the

steps.q: You save £1,000 at 2% interest but prices rise 5%. In a year, can your savings buy more or less than today?
steps.hint: Your money grew by 2%, but prices grew by 5%. Compare the two.
steps.pre: So the interest rate after allowing for price rises is the

steps.q: You borrowed £1,000 at a fixed 2% and prices rise 5% a year. Does the real value of your repayment rise or fall?
steps.right: Down, it is easier to repay in real terms
steps.wrong: Up, it is harder to repay in real terms
steps.hint: The saver just lost out from the same gap. If the saver loses, what happens to the person on the other side of that loan?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Tax bands stay fixed in cash while inflation lifts wages into a higher band. Do people pay a larger or smaller share in tax?
steps.hint: Cash wages rose, but the tax band did not move. What happens when a fixed line does not follow rising numbers?

steps.q: Pensions and benefits rise with prices, old debts stay fixed in cash, and tax bands are fixed. Does inflation leave government finances unaffected?
steps.right: It reshapes them in several ways at once
steps.hint: Tax bands, index-linked spending and old debts are all being hit by the same rising prices. Can that many channels really cancel out to nothing?
